## What is vibe-coding?

As with lots of terminology in AI boom, defining "vibe-coding" is a bit nebulous and people(/bots) use the term differently. For our purposes here, let's keep it simple as... __interacting with a LLM model in a standardised workflow such that the LLM writes the code, giving you the desired output in reproducible way.__

# Coming back to vibe-coding idea

Did you get to this point...(yes, shoehorning as many as I can😊)

![](images/module3/castle_serenity.gif){width=70%}

Now, we demonstrated vibe-coding within a Rstudio workflow with spatial data.  Obviously, vibe-coding is not restricted to spatial data and you can implement the same approach to other type of data.  At the `Agent` level, we showed <span style="color: blue;">spatial_analyst.MD</span> and <span style="color: blue;">Agents.MD</span> files.  Though created for the `Agent`, I actually found it was an useful activity to assess my workflow/approach😉

An emerging question that we are wondering about (and we mentioned in module 1...sorry to dwell) is what does this mean for how we tackle these steps in the future and our workflows. How homogenized do our workflows become?  Will there is a main spatial_analyst.MD skill that we all follow?  Do we have a project folder that has a similar structure so both humans and a local LLM that has been trained on our workflow can easily understand it, revise, and QC it?


## Strengths

![]()


| Strength | Description |
|:--|:--|
| Reproducibility | R code records each transformation, parameter and analytical decision, making the spatial workflow easier to reproduce and audit. |
| Automation | A scripted workflow can be rerun when input data change, without manually repeating each GIS operation. |
| Scalability | The same analysis can be applied consistently across many species, sites, catchments or input files. |
| Reporting integration | Maps, figures, tables and results can be generated directly in a Quarto report. |
| Reuse | Repeated spatial operations can be converted into functions or incorporated into an R package. |
| Extensibility | Once the initial workflow works, it can be expanded with loops, simulations, databases, APIs and specialist spatial packages. |


## Caveats

"The difference between two-wheel drive and four-wheel drive is how far you walk back"

big difference between __understanding__ and __being able to implement__
